title: Aging‐Induced Ductile‐Brittle‐Ductile Transition in High‐Entropy Alloys and its Implications

recollection.starting_material: Guess: a solutionized, single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy based on CoCrFeMnNi (Cantor alloy) or a closely related FeCoNiCrMn composition prepared to be carbide-lean to highlight intermetallic precipitation during aging.
recollection.intervention: Guess: isothermal aging at intermediate temperatures (roughly 650–800 C) for times from hours to tens or hundreds of hours, combined with tensile and Charpy tests, hardness measurements, and microstructural characterization (SEM/EBSD, TEM-EDS) across the aging timeline.
recollection.structure: Guess: initial single-phase FCC; during early/intermediate aging, Cr-rich intermetallic sigma (and/or mu) phase nucleates preferentially at grain boundaries, forming quasi-continuous films; intragranular nanoscale precipitates may also appear later. With prolonged aging (overaging), grain-boundary films coarsen and break up into discrete particles, while intragranular precipitates coarsen and spacing increases.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: the ductile-brittle-ductile sequence is governed by a percolation-like transition of grain-boundary intermetallics. Unaged alloy is ductile due to a clean, single-phase FCC matrix with good work hardening. Intermediate aging yields continuous or near-continuous grain-boundary sigma films that promote intergranular crack initiation and rapid propagation, causing a brittle window. Further aging breaks the continuity of grain-boundary films (coarsening and particle separation), reducing intergranular embrittlement; concurrent intragranular precipitates stabilize work hardening, so ductility partially recovers while some strength is retained.
recollection.results: Guess: strength and hardness peak at intermediate aging with severe ductility loss; for example, yield strength increases from ~200–300 MPa (solutionized) to ~700–800 MPa at peak aging while uniform/total elongation drops from ~40–50% to ~2–5%; hardness rises from ~150–180 HV to ~300–350 HV. Upon overaging, yield strength falls to ~500–600 MPa and elongation recovers to ~20–30%, with hardness decreasing toward ~250–280 HV. Fracture mode evolves from ductile dimples (unaged) to intergranular facets (peak-aged) and back to mixed or dimpled fracture (overaged). TEM/EDS shows Cr-rich sigma at grain boundaries with peak boundary coverage around the brittle regime (e.g., 50–70% areal coverage), which decreases as particles coarsen and detach during overaging.

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies intermediate-temperature aging and a ductile–brittle–ductile sequence, but this is largely evident from the title and it misses the key ~600°C embrittlement condition. It incorrectly identifies the alloy as a single-phase Cantor-type FCC alloy and attributes embrittlement to Cr-rich sigma-phase grain-boundary films. The actual material is as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC+B2 phases, and the transition is mediated by L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC boundaries, restricted cross-slip/planar slip, and ductile transition zones at ~750°C. The supplied strength, elongation, hardness, and phase-coverage values are unsupported guesses and do not match reported quantitative results.
